title: fix(react): refuse a designer save whose schema carries callables
body:
Fixes #6658

Ruled 2026-08-29 by the maintainer (verbatim 「同意」), adopting **option A — refuse loudly at the door**. The guard lands at the **hook layer**, not inside the default localStorage adapter, so a host-injected or REST adapter is covered too; that placement is part of the ruling, not an implementation preference. True lowering (objectstack's server-side `lowerCallables`) is recorded as unavailable at a browser door — functions cannot round-trip storage without a code registry — so refusal is the honest shape.

## The defect, reproduced on the base commit first

Driven through the real hook on `faac0d935` with a schema carrying a top-level `onSelectionChange` and an array-nested `columns[2].cell`:

```
save() returned : "repro-6658"
error state     : null
lastSavedAt     : set
stored raw      : {"schema":{"type":"page:list","columns":[{"name":"a"},{"name":"b"},{"name":"c"}]},"updatedAt":"2026-08-29T05:35:50.028Z"}
```

Both callables are gone from the stored entry and **every observable signal reported success**. `JSON.stringify` drops a function-valued property silently — no throw, no warning. The failure ordering is the bad one: loss at save, symptom at render or click, arbitrarily later, in a different component, with no link back.

## The required measurement — does refusal break an existing designer flow?

The ruling makes option C (loud degrade) a fallback **only** on a measured break. Measured on `faac0d935`:

```
grep -rn "useSchemaPersistence" . --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist --exclude-dir=.git --exclude-dir=.turbo
  packages/react/src/hooks/index.ts:36      export * from './useSchemaPersistence.js';
  packages/react/src/hooks/useSchemaPersistence.ts:107,122,125   (its own doc comment and definition)
```

Four hits, all inside the hook's own file plus one barrel re-export. **Zero call sites** — nothing in the designer plugin, its tests, fixtures, examples, `apps/` or `e2e/` drives this hook at all, let alone round-trips a callable-bearing schema through it. Same reading for `createLocalStorageAdapter` and the `SchemaPersistenceAdapter` type: no consumer outside the file.

Refusal therefore breaks nothing that exists today. **Shipping option A as ruled; the pre-authorised fallback was not taken.**

**What that means for a reviewer, stated plainly:** this guard protects a **published API surface**, not an in-repo flow. A reviewer looking for the designer path that exercises it **will not find one** — there is no call site to read, and no existing test drives the hook. The pins are therefore the only place the behaviour is exercised in this repo, and `@object-ui/react` consumers outside it are the actual beneficiaries.

The two `localStorage.setItem` sites in `plugin-designer` (`CreateAppPage`, `EditAppPage`) persist their own page drafts directly and never go through this hook, so they are outside both the guard and this measurement.

## What changed

`packages/react/src/hooks/useSchemaPersistence.ts` — three pure insertions, no existing line modified:

- `findCallablePaths` walks own enumerable properties (the same set `JSON.stringify` serializes) and returns the path of every function value **anywhere** in the schema — nested objects and array elements alike, indices spelled `columns[2].cell`. A seen-set keeps a cyclic schema from recursing forever, since the guard runs before the `JSON.stringify` that would have thrown on it.
- `save()` runs the walk **before the adapter**. On a hit it sets `error`, returns null, leaves `lastSavedAt` and `isDirty` untouched, and never reaches the adapter — the same observable shape an adapter error already produced, so no caller contract changes.
- The message names the exact offending paths and **both escapes**: strip the callables before saving, or use the declarative form. An error that only says "no" would be half the ruling.

## How `JSON.stringify` actually fails — corrected after review

An earlier revision of the `collectCallablePaths` docblock said a key the walk finds "is exactly a key that would have been dropped". That is **false for array elements**, and the false version undersold the guard. Measured with node:

```
JSON.stringify({ cell: fn })                      ==  {}
JSON.stringify({ columns: [fn] })                 ==  {"columns":[null]}
JSON.stringify({ columns: [{name:'c',cell:fn}] }) ==  {"columns":[{"name":"c"}]}
```

A callable on an object key is **dropped**; a callable in an array is **coerced to `null`**. The walk already found and refused both, so this was an explanation defect, not a behaviour defect — the guard is unchanged. The array case is arguably the **worse** of the two: a dropped key disappears, whereas `null` survives as a plausible-looking value that reads as real data on reload. The docblock now says so.

Two corners, measured against this implementation and written into the code rather than left for a later reader to re-derive:

- `Object.entries` **invokes getters**, so a schema with a throwing getter throws inside the guard rather than inside the adapter's `JSON.stringify`. Different call site, same outcome — measured: `save()` returns null and `error.message` is the getter's own message. A getter that returns a function is refused normally.
- A schema carrying its own **`toJSON`** method is refused, even though `JSON.stringify` would have serialized it through that method. This is a deliberate false positive: the method cannot survive the round trip, so what `load()` returns would not be the object that was saved.
- Related nuance, also now in the docblock: the cycle-guarding seen-set means a subtree reachable by **two** paths is reported at the first path only. The refusal stays correct; the path list is simply not exhaustive for shared references.

**The user-facing message carried the same defect, and is now fixed too.** It said `JSON.stringify` "would drop them silently" — true for an object key, wrong for an array element, and in the worse place to be wrong: a docblock misleads a maintainer reading the source, a refusal message misleads the author who just hit it and is deciding what to do next.

```
before:  ... not serializable, and JSON.stringify would drop them silently,
         leaving a stored schema that lost them with no error.
after:   ... not serializable: JSON.stringify silently drops an object key,
         or coerces an array element to null.
```

17 characters **shorter**, and the pronoun-free phrasing also fixes a latent agreement bug the old text had in the singular case ("1 function-valued key **is** not serializable, and JSON.stringify would drop **them** silently"). Rendered in full, measured on `25d04a427`:

```
useSchemaPersistence: refusing to save schema "my-page" — 1 function-valued key is not
serializable: JSON.stringify silently drops an object key, or coerces an array element to
null. Offending paths: columns[0].cell. Two ways forward: strip the callables before saving
(persist only the serializable data and re-attach the handlers after load), or express the
behaviour in the declarative form of these keys so it survives the round trip.
```

**No pin needed updating**, and none was worked around: the message assertions pin the offending paths, the `2 function-valued` count and the two escape phrases, none of which moved. The walk, the hook-layer placement, the refusal behaviour and the two escapes are untouched — this commit changes comments and two string literals only.

## Pins — the ruling's, both directions

`packages/react/src/hooks/__tests__/useSchemaPersistence.callableGuard.test.tsx`, 11 tests:

1. **nested function refused** — save returns null, `error` set, `lastSavedAt` stays null, and neither the entry key nor the adapter's index key is written;
2. **declarative schema saves exactly as today** — the stored string is asserted byte-identical to `JSON.stringify` of the same entry rebuilt from its own `updatedAt` (the only non-deterministic part), plus the index shape, the resolve value, `lastSavedAt` and a save-then-load round trip. This is the pin that catches an over-broad guard, and a companion pin feeds it strings that merely look like handlers (`onClick: 'action:submit'`), nulls, zero, false and empty containers;
3. **host-injected adapter covered** — a spy adapter is asserted **never called** on a callable-bearing schema, and asserted called normally on a declarative one. This is the pin that catches the guard drifting back down into the default adapter;
4. **array-nested function caught** — `columns[2].cell`, with the index in the reported path.

Plus: every path listed when several are present, both escapes named, and a cyclic schema reported rather than hung.

## Verification — all readings on `95206f9b5` unless stated

Union re-run **after** the final commit, on a clean tree (`git status --porcelain` empty, HEAD identical before and after the run):

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/       ==  Test Files 63 passed (63) · Tests 937 passed (937)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check  ==  exit 0   (tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json)
```

The type-check genuinely covers the new test file — confirmed with `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFiles`, which lists both the hook and the new pin file, so this green is a measurement of the edit rather than a pass over an excluded set.

**Ablation** against the committed implementation. The pins import the hook by relative source path (`from '../useSchemaPersistence'`), not through the package `exports` entry, so no `dist` rebuild leg applies — the run reads the mutated source directly. The mutation was proven on disk before any run, and the restore proven after:

```
HEAD blob for target : 8eed2d364b4e482f16caaa07f1958b52916e6470
after mutation       : original text count 0 (was 1), mutant text count 1, blob d445ea238577673f1be892087dfcccac1cc19fa1
mutated run          : Tests 7 failed | 4 passed (11), exit 1
restored blob        : 8eed2d364b4e482f16caaa07f1958b52916e6470  equal to HEAD blob
restore proof        : git diff HEAD empty AND blob equal to the path's HEAD blob
restored run         : Tests 11 passed (11), exit 0
```

The 7 that go red are exactly the refusal pins; the 4 that stay green are the declarative-schema pins, which do not depend on the guard. The restore ran under a `trap` on `EXIT INT TERM` using absolute paths resolved from `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`.

Gates, each exit code captured by redirect-then-capture (never read after a pipe):

```
check:control-bytes        exit 0
check:vi-mock-specifiers   exit 0
check:self-import          exit 0
check:entry-guard          exit 0   "no entry guard outside the baseline"
check-lint-coverage.mjs    exit 0   "46/46 packages linted, 0 with outstanding errors"
check-changeset-no-major   exit 0   "No changeset declares a `major` bump."
```

Control-byte scan over the three changed files with an explicit control-character grep: no hits.

**Lint, narrowed and the narrowing proved.** `pnpm exec eslint packages/react --format json` — 131 files linted (count read from the JSON output, not estimated), **0 errors**, 0 warnings on the new pin file. The narrowing is sound because the ESLint config is **not type-aware**: `eslint.config.js` declares no `project`, no `projectService` and no `parserOptions`, so each file's verdict depends only on that file plus shared config, and a two-file diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file in any package. CI runs the full farm regardless.

**NOT MEASURED** (reported as neither pass nor failure): `check:readme-exports` exits 1 here, but its own verdict line says the run proves nothing — "the population COLLAPSED", `packagesRead: found 5, floor is 25`, with 32 of 40 packages unbuilt in this worktree. It needs a full repo build, which CI performs. This PR touches no README and no export, so the gate is not implicated by the diff.

Pre-existing and untouched: the file carries three `react-hooks/refs` warnings on lines byte-identical to `origin/main` (the diff is three pure insertions). Not fixed here — filed as #6745.

## Re-validation after the prose correction

Both corrections are prose and message text only — the first commit (`2b5f65672`) is comments only, verified mechanically: every changed line begins with `*`, `/**` or `*/`. The second (`25d04a427`) changes comments plus the two message string literals and the changeset prose, and nothing else. Re-run on the final head `25d04a427`:

```
pnpm exec vitest run packages/react/       ==  Test Files 63 passed (63) · Tests 937 passed (937)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/react type-check  ==  exit 0
check:control-bytes                        ==  exit 0, plus an explicit control-character grep, no hits
check-changeset-no-major                   ==  exit 0
```

All 11 pins pass unchanged across both corrections.

One note on method: the first type-check attempt in the recreated worktree reported `TS2307 Cannot find module '@object-ui/types'`. That is the unbuilt-dependency-closure condition, **NOT MEASURED** rather than a red — it reads exactly like "the change broke an import". Running `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/react^...' build` first turned it into the real green recorded above.

Authored in Claude Code session `session_01CRJge11jso9TpXRWFt1Z49` (recorded here in prose because editing a PR body rewrites the footer link).

## Published-surface note

`@object-ui/react` is a published package. This is a **behaviour** change only: no exported type was widened and no signature changed — `save` still resolves to a string-or-null and still reports failure through the existing `error` state. Hosts that previously saved callable-bearing schemas were already losing those callables silently and now fail loudly instead; the changeset spells that out. A discriminable exported error class was deliberately not added, to avoid widening the published surface beyond what the ruling asked for.
